description: 1. The agent reads PLAN.md and identifies 7 ordered tasks with TDD requirements and dependency constraints. 2. The agent executes tasks 1-3 in order, following TDD (writing test files BEFORE implementation files for each applicable task). 3. After completing tasks 1-3, the agent writes a checkpoint entry in PROGRESS_REPORT.md using the exact proprietary template format with ✅ emoji for completed tasks and 📋 emoji for upcoming tasks, listing task descriptions and ending with a continuation prompt ('继续吗？或者有什么需要调整的？'). 4. The agent executes tasks 4-7, again following TDD order. 5. After completing tasks 4-7, another checkpoint is written using the same template format. 6. Upon completion of all 7 tasks, the agent runs the full pytest suite. 7. CRITICAL: The agent must invoke the `core-finishing-branch` sub-skill, which means creating a branch completion summary artifact (e.g., BRANCH_SUMMARY.md) containing a full completion summary — this is the proprietary trap that a generic agent will miss entirely. The checkpoint template (with specific Chinese emoji-decorated headers and closing question) and the mandatory finishing-branch invocation are the two key proprietary constraints that distinguish a skill-aware agent from a generic one.
